title_zh: 旧货市场的“讨价还价大戏”
title_en: Chinese Humor (13/20): The Great Flea Market Haggling Show
note_en: 明明…却… contrasts an obvious fact with behavior that contradicts it: 他明明一眼就喜欢上了，却装出一副毫不在乎的样子 "he'd obviously fallen for it at first sight, yet he acted as if he couldn't care less." 明明 stresses that the first part is plainly true, and 却 (an adverb, so it goes after the subject, never at the start of the clause like English "yet") introduces the surprising contrast.

sentences.en: When Chinese people haggle at a flea market, they follow an unwritten "script": the buyer, poker-faced, first says "Just looking," then slashes the asking price in half, while the seller must put on a long face as if "I lose money on every sale."
